AA-AgentPerf-Local default workload: 8 tasks, 168 model turns, 172 tool calls, tools not included in the time. Turns are sent one at a time, so concurrency is 1. Context grows to about 56K tokens. Over one run the article describes about 2.6 million prompt tokens and 31K output tokens, and about 196K new input tokens against about 31K output tokens. Those are run totals, not one request, so input_tokens, output_tokens, and context_tokens are empty. Quantization is 4-bit. The overview lists more than one 4-bit file per model and does not say which system used which, so the quantization cell stays '4-bit'. Every successful config used speculative decoding (MTP, DFlash, or DSpark). The exact engine per system was not in the fetched article, so engine is empty. task_time_s is minutes times 60. Prefill was 22 to 41 percent of completion time for Qwen3.8-27B; that is a range and is not a prefill_tok_s. AA also says speculative decoding raised Qwen3.8-27B decode about 30 to 120 percent above the bandwidth roofline; that is a range and is not stored as a token rate. After a large tool result, AA describes a pause of about 2 seconds on the RTX 5090, up to 24 seconds on the Ryzen AI Halo, and 39 seconds on the MacBook Pro. Those pauses are approximate or upper bounds and are not stored as ttft_ms. Chart label 4.9 min. Also stated in the 2026-10-26 Bruno Vega video.

Derived roofline, not a measured token rate. decode_tok_s = bandwidth_gb_s / 70, one full read of a 70 GB weight footprint at batch 1, with no KV cache. prefill_tok_s, when present, = dense_bf16_fp16_tflops * 1e12 / (2 * 70e9), the dense 16-bit peak, 2 FLOPs per parameter per token, 70 billion parameters. FP8 is not applied. Sparsity is not applied. Interconnect, overhead, and KV cache are ignored. Rounded to 3 decimal places. Bandwidth used: 1792 GB/s from this device row. This device's stated memory is 32 GB, below the 70 GB footprint, so the ceiling is not achievable for that footprint on one device.
